key_insight: By recording all four photon arrival times, the paper reveals and preserves the full temporal structure of continuous-wave four-photon Hong-Ou-Mandel interference instead of collapsing it into a single visibility number.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical benchmarking and optimization tool for photonic quantum network systems, letting engineers tune coincidence windows to balance interference visibility against usable count rate.
method: Generate long-coherence photon pairs in microring resonators under continuous-wave pumping
Use ultrafast time-resolved detection to record all four arrival times
Map relative delays into a 3D coincidence histogram referenced to a trigger detection
evidence_signal: The abstract reports modeled and measured four-photon interference patterns with time-resolved 3D histograms, enabling post-processed coincidence-window optimization to trade off visibility versus count rate.
watch_item: The approach relies on ultrafast timing resolution and post-processing, so performance may depend strongly on detector jitter, timing calibration, and experimental stability.
paper_title: Looking Beyond Visibility: Resolving the Temporal Structure of Continuous-Wave Four-Photon Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
